story.iWant: to record my screen and webcam simultaneously with a single click
story.soThat: I can create tutorials with my face visible without complex setup
story.tasks: - Implement PiP mode initialization (AC: 1, 2) - Acquire screen stream with audio (AC: 4) - Acquire webcam stream with audio (AC: 5) - Create dual MediaRecorder instances (AC: 3, 4, 5) - Implement synchronized start (AC: 6, 7) - Implement synchronized stop (AC: 8) - Save both output files (AC: 9, 10) - Implement graceful fallback (AC: 11) - Handle partial recording failures (AC: 12) - Implement comprehensive logging (AC: 13) - Clean up resources properly - Write integration tests - Manual testing with real devices

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: RecordingService.startRecording() handles 'pip' mode by orchestrating both screen and webcam recording
Both screen and webcam sources auto-selected (primary screen + default webcam)
Two separate MediaRecorder instances created and started simultaneously
Both recordings start within 2 seconds of mode selection (NFR requirement)
Both recordings buffered independently with 5s timeslice for crash recovery
Recording stop triggers both recorders to stop simultaneously
RecordingService.stopRecording() returns both file paths with metadata
Graceful fallback: if webcam unavailable, fall back to screen-only with user notification
Error handling for partial failures (e.g., screen succeeds, webcam fails)
Comprehensive logging for PiP orchestration with [Recording] prefix

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: PiP is the highlighted/default mode. User clicks "Screen + Webcam (PiP)", system auto-selects both sources, creates two MediaRecorder instances, saves two separate WebM files, auto-imports both, auto-places screen on Track 1 and webcam on Track 2 with 20% size, bottom-right, circular.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Two separate files saved, NOT composited during recording. Compositing happens later in timeline/preview. Webcam overlay position applied in timeline, not during capture.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Concurrent recording: PiP mode must handle 2 simultaneous MediaRecorder instances without performance degradation. Combined memory usage <500MB for 10-minute recording.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Graceful degradation: if webcam unavailable, PiP mode falls back to screen-only with user notification.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Shows orchestration: startRecording('pip') → auto-select sources → create both recorders → start simultaneously → buffer chunks → stopRecording → stop both → save two files → return both paths.

artifact.reason: Combines Stories 5.3 (screen) and 5.4 (webcam) logic. Orchestrates dual MediaRecorder instances, synchronized start/stop, fallback logic, dual file saving.

node.package: Provides both desktopCapturer (screen) and getUserMedia context (webcam)

constraints.constraint: NO Canvas compositing during recording - saves two separate files
Compositing happens later in timeline/preview (Story 4.7 from Epic 4)
Same timestamp used for both filenames for easy matching
Webcam overlay position (bottom-right, 20%, circle) applied in timeline, NOT during capture
Microphone audio goes to screen recording
Webcam audio goes to webcam recording
Both recorders must start within 2 seconds total
Fallback to screen-only if webcam unavailable (graceful degradation)
If screen fails, abort completely (screen is primary)
If webcam fails during recording, continue screen-only with notification

interface.name: RecordingOutput for PiP

tests.standards: Unit tests with mocked screen and webcam APIs. Test synchronized start/stop timing. Test dual file output. Test fallback scenarios without hardware removal. Manual testing critical for real dual-device behavior, permission flows, performance under load.
